newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - MG buys BHF stake in AGIV.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - MG buys BHF stake in AGIV.

text.p: Metallgesellschaft AG (MG) said on Monday it planned to buy a 49.99 percent stake in AGIV from BHF-Bank AG in a bid to gain managerial control of the loss-making industrial holding company.
The price to be paid for the stake was not revealed and the transaction has yet to be approved by the companies' supervisory boards and by cartel authorities.
All three firms said they would benefit from the transaction and their shares jumped in reaction to the news.

AGIV was the main gainer, closing up 10 percent or 2.50 marks at 27.50 marks by the close of trade. BHF shares rose two percent or 0.80 marks to 39.30 marks and MG shares ended up 3.3 percent or 1.10 marks at 34 marks.

MG, a diversified industrial group rescued from the brink of bankruptcy in 1993, said the addition of AGIV would strengthen its plant construction business and create a new division in process control and measuring technology.
"The transaction increases the inner value of the MG share," MG chief executive Kajo Neukirchen said in a statement.
BHF-Bank, whose earnings last year were hit by AGIV's decision to omit its dividend, said it was selling the stake to streamline its portfolio of industrial investments.
AGIV chief executive Udo Stark said he expected the purchase to boost his group's earnings.

AGIV, whose full name is AGIV Aktiengesellschaft fuer Industrie und Verkehrswesen, has said it made an operating loss of about 40 million marks in 1996 but predicted a turnaround in 1997 through the sale of activities in a restructuring.
AGIV omitted its dividend payment for last year, hitting BHF's net interest income which fell about two percent in the first six months of 1996.

The company, whose businesses comprise mechanical engineering, electronics, electrical engineering, power supply, construction and transport, expects its annual sales to fall to about 6.5 billion marks by the end of the restructuring in 1998 from about 9.6 billion marks now.

AGIV aims to concentrate its activities on engineering, electronics and technical services. It said at the end of 1996 that it was selling its 74 percent stake in building group Wayss & Freytag to Dutch-based Hollandsche Beton Groep NV.
An MG spokesman said MG planned to take managerial control of industrial holding company AGIV but declined to comment on whether it planned to increase its stake beyond 49.99 percent.

MG does not own any AGIV shares yet. Given the fact that less than 100 percent of a company's capital usually attends annual general meetings in Germany, a stake of 49.99 percent would in theory be sufficient to secure a majority of shareholder votes.
Energieversorgung Schwaben AG, a regional utility, holds more than 10 percent of AGIV. About 40 percent of the shares are widely distributed.
AGIV shares leaped three marks ($1.89) to 28.30 on the news in pre-bourse electronic trade.
